decisions.reason: The new main-board button connector taps the existing PWRON line on J_PWR_SIG pin 4; it does not change the interboard connector or its pinout.
The panel-mounted power button is separate from the ESP32 BOOT button and J_RESET circuit.
Moving the power-button connector to the main board does not alter standalone USB regulation, source selection, or powered loads.
The source changes only the power-button connector placement and PWRON tap; rail-current monitoring remains unchanged.
Using the existing AXP2101 PWRON signal for a panel button does not change the battery or USB power-path topology.
The source concerns a separate power-button connector and does not change battery-connector placement, orientation, or clearance.
The client avoids adding the button connector to the power board; none of the recorded power-board mechanical constraints are changed.
Adding a connector to an existing PWRON line does not change the selected ESP32-S3 module.
The panel power-button connection does not affect USB enumeration or programming.
PWRON is tapped from an existing interboard signal and the source establishes no ESP32 GPIO reassignment.
The PWRON connector change does not affect I2C pull-ups, series resistors, bus speed, or cable constraints.
The source resolves only the panel power-button connector location; the client treats DCDC1 output voltage as a separate unresolved question.
